svg.title: The instant lane
svg.desc: How a call is routed to the instant lane or to a claim, and where the money goes in an instant deposit and an instant redeem: a fee to a recipient, a retained part that stays in the escrow for the existing holders.
svg.text: Which path does a call take?
Deposit and mint look at the deposit side, withdraw and redeem at the redeem side.
Example: price 1 and a 1% fee on the gross amount. The pool's instant policy picks one of two homes for the fee.
A fee recipient is set: the fee is paid out
No recipient: the fee stays in the escrow
shares = (paid - fee) / price either way. A retained fee reaches the escrow but backs no shares, so the holders already there own it.
Instant redeem: shares worth 1000 are burned
A fee recipient is set: the fee is paid out
No recipient: the fee stays in the escrow
The shares burn at their full value either way, so a retained fee
stays in the escrow and accrues to the holders who stay.
fee = fee bps of the gross, rounded up. mint and withdraw are the exact-out forms: the policy grosses the net up, rounding up.
A negative fee is a rebate paid by the fee recipient, so it needs one; the shipped policy never answers one.
